info.title: CloudDrive API
info.description: Self-hosted file storage server with folder organisation, resumable uploads, thumbnails, shared links and LAN-aware download URLs.

details.description: Optional machine-readable context, e.g. quota_bytes/used_bytes/needed_bytes on quota_exceeded

trash_retention_days.description: Days a trashed file is kept before auto-purge. 0 = auto-purge disabled.

purge_at.description: When this trashed item will be permanently purged. Only present on GET /trash when server-side retention is enabled.

local_url.description: LAN download URL (omitted if server has no detected LAN IP)

breadcrumb.description: Ancestor chain from root to this folder

FileCursorList.description: Returned instead of FileList whenever the request includes `limit` and/or `cursor`.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; null when there are no more results.

folder_id.description: Destination folder. Required semantics only apply to op=move.

get.description: No auth, no DB access. Used by clients to confirm a typed server URL is actually a CloudDrive box, measure latency for LAN-vs-WAN detection, and distinguish "server down" from "wrong network".

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new access + refresh token pair
post.description: The supplied refresh token is immediately revoked and replaced. Store the new pair.

get.summary: Get current user info including quota and storage usage
Get server LAN IP addresses for direct local transfers
get.description: No authentication required. Clients on the same LAN should prefer local_url from file responses.

post.description: For files larger than ~100 MB prefer the resumable upload flow at /uploads/resumable.

201.description: File stored. url and local_url point to the download endpoint.

get.summary: List root-level files (not inside any folder)

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor. Supplying this (or limit) switches the response shape to FileCursorList.

200.description: File list — FileList by default, FileCursorList when limit and/or cursor are supplied

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Substring to search for in filename

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Narrow results to a mime-type category, applied server-side.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor. Supplying this (or limit) switches the response shape to FileCursorList.

200.description: Matching files (FileList for page/limit, FileCursorList when cursor/limit-cursor mode is used)

get.summary: Get file metadata and download URLs

patch.description: All fields are optional. Send only what you want to change. Set folder_id to null to move to root.

folder_id.description: Destination folder ID. null = move to root.

delete.description: File is not permanently removed. Use DELETE /trash/{id} to purge.

get.description: Returns 202 while the thumbnail is still being generated, 422 if generation failed.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before polling again

post.summary: Create a public share link for a file

expires_in.description: Link lifetime in seconds. Omit for a link that never expires.

get.summary: Download a file using a share token (no auth required)
List all files that have a ready thumbnail

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Narrow results to a mime-type category, applied server-side.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor. Supplying this (or limit) switches the response shape to FileCursorList.

parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor. Supplying this (or limit) switches the response shape to FileCursorList.

200.description: Trashed files. Items include purge_at when server-side retention is enabled.

delete.summary: Permanently delete all of my trashed files
delete.description: Irreversible. Powers the "Free up space" flow.

post.summary: Restore a trashed file to its original location

delete.summary: Permanently delete a trashed file from storage
delete.description: This is irreversible. The file is removed from SeaweedFS and the database.

post.description: Creates a session and returns an upload_id. Then PATCH chunks using Content-Range headers.

get.summary: List my open (unexpired) resumable upload sessions
get.description: Lets a client rediscover in-flight uploads after a crash, reinstall, or on a second device, without having persisted the upload_id itself.
Use this after a dropped connection to find the current offset before resuming.

patch.description:
Send raw bytes with a Content-Range header. Repeat until 201 is returned.

Content-Range format: `bytes <start>-<end>/<total>`

Returns 200 with updated offset while upload is incomplete, 201 with the new file record when complete.

200.description: Chunk received, upload still in progress

post.description: Omit parent_id for a root folder. Nesting is unlimited.

get.summary: Get folder contents — subfolders, files and breadcrumb path

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor. Supplying this (or limit) switches the response shape to FileCursorList.

delete.description: Returns 409 if the folder still contains files or subfolders.

get.description: Security-audit surface: "what have I exposed publicly?" Returns only the caller's own unexpired links — server truth, never client-cached.

post.summary: Apply move/trash/restore/delete to multiple files in one request
post.description: Per-item execution (no cross-item transaction). Always returns a 207 body listing which ids succeeded and which failed, so the client can render a coherent partial-failure result instead of fanning out N sequential requests. Max 100 ids per request. `delete` and `restore` operate on trashed files, matching DELETE /trash/{id} and POST /trash/{id}/restore.

400.description: Validation error (bad op, empty ids, or over the 100-item cap)
